JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 10-12-2022 at about 1.50 a.m., the petitioner was driving his car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-P-5468 along with his family members.

When they were proceeding near Anchoor Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Krishnagiri to Tiruvannamalai N.H. road, at that time the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the car of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Krishnagiri, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru for treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment.
Earlier to the accident, he was running a mobile shop at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per annum.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kandhikuppam Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tempo Traveler, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, on 10-12-2022 at about 1.50 a.m., the tempo traveler bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-AF-4030 was driven by its driver very carefully, constantly, observing all traffic rules,
near Anchoor Indian Petrol Bunk, Krishnagiri to Tiruvannamalai N.H. road.

At that time, the Manjunatha R vs Jaganathan A on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123101814/
2 petitioner was driving his car with high speed, in rash and negligently manner, without following any traffic rules and dashed against the Tempo traveler.

For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
Further, it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act and barred by limitation.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P- 5468, who was driving the same at high speed, in negligent manner, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident.

Further it is contended that, the liability of the respondent No.2 if any, in respect of the Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030, is subject to the driver of said vehicle having proper, valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, it has got valid permit and fitness certificate as on the alleged date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, arose out of the usage of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.

No.KA-01-AF-4030 on the public road, alleged to have occurred on 10-12-2022 at about 1.50 a.m.,
near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Krishnagiri-Tiruvannamalai N.H. Road, within the jurisdiction of Kandhikuppam Police Station, Krishnagiri District, Tamil Nadu ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has got examined its representative/Senior Legal Manager and First Division Assistant of R.T.O. Whereas, the respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Negative.

REASONS 10.
Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-12-2022 at about 1.50 a.m., when the petitioner was driving his car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468 along with his family members, near Anchoor Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Krishnagiri to Tiruvannamalai N.H. road, the driver of offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the car of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Krishnagiri, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, for treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was running a mobile shop at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per annum.

But,
due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 9 documents as Ex.P.1 to 9.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 and 1(a) are certified copy of F.I.R. and its translation copy,
Ex.P.2 and 2(a) are certified copy of first information statement and its translation copy, Ex.P.3 and 3(a) are certified copy of spot mahazar and its translation copy, Ex.P.4 and 5 are certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident reports (total 2), Ex.P.6 is true copy of accident register, Ex.P7 and 7(a) are certified copy of charge-sheet and its translation copy, Ex.P.8 is notarized copy of driving licence and Ex.P.9 is certified copy of sketch.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7 and 9,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner/driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468 and dashing the same to the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030, which was proceeding on the left side of the road.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner/driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468.

At the outset it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030 and car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-P-5468 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said Tempo Traveler and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
The respondents No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident.

Further, the respondent No.1 has taken specific contentions that, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner/driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of said Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030.
In order to establish the same, the respondent No.2 has examined its representative/Senior Legal Manager as R.W.1.

The R.W.1 has deposed in his evidence affidavit that, the accident in question has taken place due to sole negligence of the petitioner himself, as the petitioner being the driver of car bearing No. KA-05-P-5468, drove the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030.
No doubt, except the self serving statements of R.W.1, there is no other independent oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2, to establish the said contentions.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the documents produced and got marked by the petitioner himself, clearly goes to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident the petitioner was driving his car at high speed and in rash and negligent manner and due to his own negligence the said accident has occurred.
The entire investigation documents available on record clearly reveals that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner and he himself is a tort-feasor.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner/driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468 and he himself has dashed to the Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AF-4030, which was proceeding on the left side of the road.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the petitioner.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P- 5468 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the petitioner.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.9 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side on Krishnagiri-Tiruvannamalai National Highway road, near Anchoor Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, within the jurisdiction of Kandhikuppam Police Station,
Krishnagiri District, Tamil Nadu, in between car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468 and Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports,
which are marked as Ex.P.4 and 5, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner/driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 charge- sheet/final report has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner/driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-P-5468.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that, the petitioner is seeking compensation under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, for the injuries sustained in the present accident, arose out of the usage of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF- 4030.

It is settled proposition of law that, under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant need not require to establish that, the injury is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the opposite vehicle involved in the accident or of the concerned or of any other person.
But they have to prove the involvement of said vehicle in the alleged accident, resulting in the injury or death of a person.

The Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, reads as follows:
164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc. - (1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
(2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.
(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section.
16.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes the involvement of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-01-AF-4030 in the said accident and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in said.

As per Ex.P.6 accident register, the petitioner has sustained 1) laceration of size 5x3x1 cm over left knee, 2) abrasion of size 3x2 cm and 2x1 cm over left knee with restricted range of motion, 3) abrasion of size 3x1 cm over left parietal scalp and 4)
laceration of size 1x0.5 cm over left eye-lid.
There is absolutely no document produced by the petitioner to show that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner has failed to prove that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident taken place on 10-12-2022 at about 1:50 a.m.,
on Krishnagiri-Tiruvannamalai National Highway road, near Anchoor Indian Oil Petrol Bunk,
within the jurisdiction of Kandhikuppam Police Station, Krishnagiri District, Tamil Nadu, arose out of the usage of Tempo Traveler bearing registration No.KA-01-AF-4030 on the public road.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Negative.
17. Issue No.2:

In view of conclusion arrived on Issue No.1 and as there is no provision under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicle Act, to grant compensation to victim who has suffered simple injuries, this Court declines to grant any compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Negative.
